turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.

I know who you are, Hale. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. I have a call at 4:40, so tell me who decided on that zero, and on what basis.
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
"We." Who is "we", Hale, and did any of you speak to Owen before that zero went in? Go ahead, walk me through it.
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.

11:31 PM, the night before it was due, I'm writing that down. A file created that night tells you when a document was opened, not who wrote the words or where his drafts were, and nobody called me before that zero went in, which is 4.2 in your own procedure. Turn the screen so I can read that history myself.
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.

612 at 11:52, 794 at 11:58, "mostly in one paste", I've got it down. Pasting from his own notes is still pasting, Hale, and you entered a zero before you heard a word from Owen or from me. Show me the screen, then tell me under which section of your procedure that zero went in first.
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
Save it, Hale, I'm not here to be respected. Turn the screen, and answer my question: which section?
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.

"Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings," I'm writing that down, and I'll look for it in the play tonight myself. Seventeen-year-olds misremember lines and paraphrase all the time, Hale, so a bad quotation is a bad quotation. Which three editions, and is that line in his essay as a direct quote, marked as Shakespeare's words?
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Don't manage me, Hale. Which three editions, and is it in quotation marks as Shakespeare's?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.

An October 15 outline, cowardice, and the final essay says moral caution. Changing his mind between an outline and a final draft is what an outline is for, Hale. Put the outline and the essay in front of me side by side, with the date on the outline, and I'll read them properly.
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.

A machine's guess, Hale, and Turnitin's own guide, which is printed and in my bag, says it "should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student." Your own 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish anything either. You've told me about a file history, a quotation, and an outline, and I haven't seen one of them, so turn the screen.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
There's no off the record, Hale, and you're asking me how to do your job. Take the zero off and show me what you have.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.

Ten minutes. If that's 4.4, the rewrite's mark replaces the zero, it's private, and nothing goes on his record, all in writing tonight. I'm not agreeing to a rewrite for anything until I've read what you've been describing, Hale.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? Eight minutes, Hale. The screen.
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.

Go ahead, Hale, I'm going to the principal tonight anyway, and then the board under section 42. Put "the zero stands" in writing so I have it in your words. And you still haven't shown me a single page.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Neither. The zero comes off, Hale, because it went in before anyone called me. Show me those pages and we can talk about anything else.
